name: Sublime Text
tagline: A fast native code editor with fuzzy file navigation, multi-cursor editing and a large package ecosystem.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Sold as a perpetual license with a separate per-user business option, so a monthly figure does not apply.

verdictSummary: An agent can absolutely produce a working text editor in a session: open a file, edit it, save it, fuzzy-find across a folder. What it cannot produce is the thing people actually pay for, which is a hand-tuned native rendering and buffer engine that stays instant on a 200MB log file and cold-starts before you notice. Sublime's value is measured in milliseconds and in twenty years of behavioral detail: multi-cursor semantics, incremental syntax definitions, project-wide search that finishes, and Package Control. A CodeMirror-in-a-webview clone is a fine toy and will be a worse editor than the free options you already have. Build it to learn, not to switch.
coreLoopDIY: A local desktop editor with a file tree, tabs, syntax highlighting, multi-cursor editing and fuzzy Goto Anything over the open folder.
requirements: Rust toolchain and Node for a Tauri build
A local folder to open as a project
Nothing else: no accounts, no network
whatYouLose: Native performance: huge files, instant startup, no webview jank
The package ecosystem and Package Control, which is most of the real configurability
Mature syntax definitions, symbol indexing and project-wide search that scales
Multi-cursor and selection semantics that have been refined for two decades
Cross platform builds, code signing and an editor that survives your OS updating
moatNotes: The engine is the product. Everything visible is a thin shell over years of profiling.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a license is cheap relative to the number of hours people spend inside an editor, and because nothing else feels quite like it under load. The people who pay are usually the ones who tried the free alternatives, hit a 100k-line file or a slow project search, and came back. Muscle memory and a settings file they have been carrying between machines for a decade do the rest.
notes: You can build an editor in a weekend; you cannot build this one. The moat is a hand-optimized native engine plus twenty years of keystroke-level behavior that users have wired into their hands.
prompt:
Build a minimal local code editor as a desktop app. This is a learning build, not a Sublime Text replacement.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Tauri v2 with a Rust backend
- Frontend: TypeScript, Vite, no framework, plain DOM
- Editor component: CodeMirror 6
- No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics

Features in scope:
1. Open a folder. Show a collapsible file tree in a left sidebar, reading the tree from Rust via a Tauri command. Respect .gitignore and skip node_modules and .git.
2. Tabs. Click a file to open it in a tab. Dirty tabs get a dot. Cmd/Ctrl+S saves, Cmd/Ctrl+W closes.
3. CodeMirror 6 editor with line numbers, bracket matching, and language support for JS, TS, JSON, Markdown, Python, HTML, CSS, Rust.
4. Multi-cursor: enable CodeMirror's built-in multiple selections plus Cmd/Ctrl+D to add the next occurrence of the current selection.
5. Goto Anything: Cmd/Ctrl+P opens a fuzzy file palette. Do the file walk and fuzzy scoring in Rust, return the top 50 matches, render in a floating overlay with arrow keys and Enter.
6. Project-wide find: Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F runs a plain substring search in Rust across text files under the project root, streams results to the UI, click a result to open the file at that line.
7. Settings: a single settings.json in the app config dir for font size, tab size, theme (dark or light). Reload on save.

Explicitly out of scope: LSP, autocomplete, debugging, git integration, a plugin system, terminal, remote editing, split panes.

Rust side rules: never read a file over 5MB into the editor, show a placeholder instead. All filesystem paths must be validated to stay inside the opened project root.

Deliverables: working `npm run tauri dev`, a README with keybindings, and a HONEST-LIMITS.md listing what this will never do as well as a native editor.
